correctness.rationale: For connected unit-edge capped bipartite graphs, C=2R-I, and an M-matrix ensures strictly positive offdiagonals. A coefficientwise positive Neumann-walk lift compares base-graph and universal-cover diagonal resolvents; inverse Loewner monotonicity compares cover and completed biregular tree. Exact two-cavity Schur complements yield a unique physical root threshold and prove the degree-p root is worst. The threshold quadratic has one positive root; strong-resolvent convergence of finite balls proves every above-threshold counterexample. No finite computation replaces universal steps; 45 algebraic checks, 45 root tests and 223 exact graph inverses replayed.
